readings.title: Functional Trust and the Victory of the Eastern Tribes
readings.subtitle: By exercising Emunah in battle, the tribes of Re’uḇěn, Gaḏ, and Menashsheh leaned their full weight upon Elohim, establishing a hedge of protection and absolute victory.
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 5:18] The sons of Re’uḇěn, and the Gaḏites, and half the tribe of Menashsheh had forty-four thousand seven hundred and sixty brave men, men able to bear shield and sword, to shoot with the bow, and skilled in battle, going out to the army. [19] And they fought against the Haḡrites, and Yetur, and Naphish, and Noḏaḇ. [20] And they were helped against them, and the Haḡrites were given into their hand, and all who were with them. For they cried out to <dn>Elohim</dn> in the battle, and <dn>He</dn> answered their prayer, because they put their trust in <dn>Him</dn>. [21] And they took away their livestock: fifty thousand of their camels, and two hundred and fifty thousand of their sheep, and two thousand of their donkeys, also one hundred thousand of their men, [22] for many fell dead, because the battle was of <dn>Elohim</dn>. And they dwelt in their place until the exile.

readings.title: The Breach of Covenant and the Adversarial Tool
readings.subtitle: The tribes abandoned the cosmic architecture of YeHoVaH for localized idols, prompting the Creator to deploy the sovereign of Ashshur as a regulated tool of judgment.
readings.text: [23] And the children of the half-tribe of Menashsheh dwelt in the land. They increased from Bashan to Ba‛al Ḥermon, that is, to Senir, or Mount Ḥermon. [24] And these were the heads of their fathers’ houses: Ěpher, and Yishi, and Eli’ěl, and Azri’ěl, and Yirmeyah, Hoḏavyah, and Yaḥdi’ěl – mighty brave men, men of name, and heads of their fathers’ houses. [25] But they trespassed against the <dn>Elohim</dn> of their fathers, and whored after the mighty ones of the peoples of the land, whom <dn>Elohim</dn> had destroyed before them. [26] So the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl stirred up <dn>את</dn> the spirit of Pul sovereign of Ashshur, even <dn>את</dn> the spirit of Tiglath-Pileser sovereign of Ashshur. And <dn>he</dn> took the Re’uḇěnites, and the Gaḏites, and the half-tribe of Menashsheh into exile, and brought them to Ḥalaḥ, and Ḥaḇor, and Hara, and the river of Gozan, unto this day.

readings.title: The Qadosh Lineage of the High Priest
readings.subtitle: The exact, successive lineage of Aharon, exclusively reserved to maintain the prescribed mechanics of atonement and cosmic harmony for Yisra’ěl.
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 6:3] ...And the sons of Aharon: Naḏaḇ and Aḇihu, El‛azar and Ithamar. [4] El‛azar brought forth Pineḥas, Pineḥas brought forth Aḇishua; [5] and Aḇishua brought forth Buqqi, and Buqqi brought forth Uzzi; [6] and Uzzi brought forth Zeraḥyah, and Zeraḥyah brought forth Merayoth; [7] Merayoth brought forth Amaryah, and Amaryah brought forth Aḥituḇ; [8] and Aḥituḇ brought forth Tsaḏoq, and Tsaḏoq brought forth Aḥima‛ats; [9] and Aḥima‛ats brought forth Azaryah, and Azaryah brought forth Yoḥanan; [10] and Yoḥanan brought forth Azaryah – it was <dn>he</dn> who served as priest in the House that Shelomoh built in Yerushalayim; [11] and Azaryah brought forth Amaryah, and Amaryah brought forth Aḥituḇ; [12] and Aḥituḇ brought forth Tsaḏoq, and Tsaḏoq brought forth Shallum; [13] and Shallum brought forth Ḥilqiyah, and Ḥilqiyah brought forth Azaryah; [14] and Azaryah brought forth Serayah, and Serayah brought forth Yehotsaḏaq. [15] And Yehotsaḏaq went away when <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> sent Yehuḏah and Yerushalayim into exile by the hand of Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar. [49] But Aharon and <dn>his</dn> sons offered on the slaughter-place of ascending offering and on the slaughter-place of incense, for all the work of the Most Set-apart Place, and to make atonement for Yisra’ěl, according to all that Mosheh the servant of <dn>Elohim</dn> had commanded.

readings.title: The Mighty Men of Yissasḵar
readings.subtitle: A strictly organized, functional structure of brave men mapped by their generation and capability for battle.
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 7:1] And the sons of Yissasḵar: Tola, and Pu’ah, Yashuḇ, and Shimron, four. [2] And the sons of Tola: Uzzi, and Rephayah, and Yeri’ěl, and Yaḥmai, and Yiḇsam, and Shemu’ěl, heads of their father’s house. Of Tola there were great men of might in their generations; their number in the days of Daviḏ was twenty-two thousand six hundred. [3] And the son of Uzzi: Yizraḥyah, and the sons of Yizraḥyah: Miḵa’ěl, and Oḇaḏyah, and Yo’ěl, Yishshiyah. All five of them were heads. [4] And with them, by their generations, according to their fathers’ houses, were thirty-six thousand, bands of the army for battle, for they had many wives and sons. [5] And their brothers among all the clans of Yissasḵar were mighty brave men, listed by their genealogies, eighty-seven thousand in all.

readings.title: Binyamin's Warriors and Houses
readings.subtitle: Heads of their fathers' houses, established as men of valor within the broader tribal architecture.
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 7:6] Of Binyamin: Bela, and Beḵer, and Yeḏiya’ěl, three. [7] And the sons of Bela: Etsbon, and Uzzi, and Uzzi’ěl, and Yerimoth, and Iri, five – heads of their fathers’ houses, and they were listed by their genealogies, twenty-two thousand and thirty-four mighty brave men. [8] And the sons of Beḵer: Zemirah, and Yo‛ash, and Eli‛ezer, and Elyo‛ěynai, and Omri, and Yerimoth, and Aḇiyah, and Anathoth, and Alemeth. All these were the sons of Beḵer, [9] with their genealogy according to their generations, heads of their fathers’ houses, twenty thousand two hundred mighty brave men. [10] And the son of Yeḏiya’ěl: Bilhan, and the sons of Bilhan: Ye‛ush, and Binyamin, and Ěhuḏ, and Kena‛anah, and Zěthan, and Tarshish, and Aḥishaḥar. [11] All these sons of Yeḏiya’ěl were heads of their fathers’ houses, seventeen thousand two hundred mighty brave men going out to the army for battle. [12] And Shuppim and Ḥuppim were the sons of Ir, and Ḥushim was the son of Aḥěr.

readings.title: The Sons of Bilhah
readings.subtitle: A brief genealogical record of Naphtali's direct lineage.
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 7:13] The sons of Naphtali: Yaḥtsi’ěl, and Guni, and Yětser, and Shallum, sons of Bilhah.

readings.title: The Lineage Through Maḵir
readings.subtitle: Tracing the specific tribal descendants of Menashsheh and their inherited territories.
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 7:14] The sons of Menashsheh: <dn>his</dn> Aramean concubine bore <dn>him</dn> Maḵir the father of Gil‛aḏ, the father of Asri’ěl. [15] And Maḵir took wives for Ḥuppim and Shuppim; and the name of one was Ma‛aḵah, and the name of the second was Tselophḥaḏ. And Tselophḥaḏ had daughters. [16] But Ma‛aḵah the wife of Maḵir bore a son, and she called <dn>his</dn> name Peresh. And the name of <dn>his</dn> brother was Sheresh, and <dn>his</dn> sons were Ulam and Raqem. [17] And the son of Ulam: Beḏan. These were the sons of Gil‛aḏ, son of Maḵir, son of Menashsheh. [18] And <dn>his</dn> sister Hammoleḵeth bore Ishhod, and Aḇi‛ezer, and Maḥlah. [19] And the sons of Shemiḏa: Aḥyan, and Sheḵem, and Liqḥi, and Aniyam.

readings.title: Ephrayim's Loss and Expansion
readings.subtitle: The tragic loss of Ephrayim's sons to men of Gath, the subsequent mourning, and the eventual geographical expansion of his lineage.
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 7:20] And the sons of Ephrayim: Shuthelaḥ, and Bereḏ <dn>his</dn> son, and Taḥath <dn>his</dn> son, and Elaḏah <dn>his</dn> son, and Taḥath <dn>his</dn> son, [21] and Zaḇaḏ <dn>his</dn> son, and Shuthelaḥ <dn>his</dn> son, and Ezer and El‛aḏ. But the men of Gath who were born in that land killed them because they came down to take their livestock. [22] And Ephrayim their father mourned many days, and <dn>his</dn> brothers came to comfort <dn>him</dn>. [23] And when <dn>he</dn> went in to <dn>his</dn> wife, she conceived and bore a son. And <dn>he</dn> called <dn>his</dn> name Beri‛ah, because evil had come upon <dn>his</dn> house. [24] And <dn>his</dn> daughter was She‛erah, who built Lower and Upper Běyth Ḥoron and Uzzen She‛erah. [25] And Rephaḥ was <dn>his</dn> son, as well as Resheph, and Telaḥ <dn>his</dn> son, and Taḥan <dn>his</dn> son, [26] La‛dan <dn>his</dn> son, Ammihuḏ <dn>his</dn> son, Elishama <dn>his</dn> son, [27] Nun <dn>his</dn> son, Yehoshua <dn>his</dn> son. [28] And their possessions and dwelling places were Běyth Ěl and its towns: to the east Na‛aran, and to the west Gezer and its towns, and Sheḵem and its towns, as far as Ayyah and its towns. [29] And by the borders of the children of Menashsheh were Běyth She’an and its towns, Ta‛anaḵ and its towns, Meḡiddo and its towns, Dor and its towns. In these dwelt the children of Yosěph, son of Yisra’ěl.

readings.title: The Chosen Leaders of Ashěr
readings.subtitle: Chosen men, strictly mapped by genealogy, fully equipped and capable of executing high-level military tasks within the structural framework of Yisra’ěl.
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 7:30] The sons of Ashěr: Yimnah, and Yishvah, and Yishvi, and Beri‛ah, and their sister Seraḥ. [31] And the sons of Beri‛ah: Ḥeḇer and Malki’ěl, who was the father of Birzoth. [32] And Ḥeḇer brought forth Yaphlět, and Shoměr, and Ḥotham, and their sister Shuva. [33] And the sons of Yaphlět: Pasaḵ, and Bimhal, and Ashvath. These were the children of Yaphlět. [34] And the sons of Shemer: Aḥi, and Rohagah, Yeḥubbah, and Aram. [35] And the sons of <dn>his</dn> brother Ḥělem: Tsophaḥ, and Yimna, and Shelesh, and Amal. [36] The sons of Tsophaḥ: Suvah, and Ḥarnepher, and Shu‛al, and Běri, and Yimrah, [37] Betser, and Hoḏ, and Shamma, and Shilshah, and Yithran, and Be’ěra. [38] And the sons of Yether: Yephunneh, and Pispah, and Ara. [39] And the sons of Ulla: Araḥ, and Ḥanni’ěl, and Ritsya. [40] All these were the children of Ashěr, heads of their fathers’ houses, chosen ones, mighty brave men, chief leaders. And when they registered by genealogy for the army, for battle, their number was twenty-six thousand.

readings.title: Binyamin’s Exiled Offspring
readings.subtitle: Tracking the specific movements, exiles, and resettlements of Binyamin's descendants across diverse regions, including the fields of Mo'aḇ.
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 8:1] And Binyamin brought forth Bela <dn>his</dn> first-born, Ashběl the second, Aḥraḥ the third, [2] Noḥah the fourth, and Rapha the fifth. [3] And the sons of Bela: Addar, and Gěra, and Aḇihuḏ, [4] and Aḇishua, and Na‛aman, and Aḥovaḥ, [5] and Gěra, and Shephuphan, and Ḥuram. [6] And these are the sons of Ěḥuḏ. They were the heads of the fathers’ houses of the inhabitants of Geḇa, and they were exiled to Manaḥath. [7] And Na‛aman, and Aḥiyah, and Gěra – <dn>he</dn> exiled them. And Ěḥuḏ brought forth Uzza and Aḥihuḏ. [8] And Shaḥarayim brought forth children in the field of Mo’aḇ, after <dn>he</dn> had sent away Ḥushim and Ba‛ara <dn>his</dn> wives. [9] And by Ḥoḏesh <dn>his</dn> wife <dn>he</dn> brought forth Yoḇaḇ, and Tsiḇya, and Měysha, and Malkam, [10] and Ye‛uts, and Shoḇyah, and Mirmah. These were <dn>his</dn> sons, heads of their fathers’ houses. [11] And by Ḥushim <dn>he</dn> brought forth Aḇituḇ and Elpa‛al. [12] And the sons of Elpa‛al: Ěḇer, and Mish‛am, and Shemer, who built Ono and Loḏ with its towns;

readings.title: The Inhabitants of Yerushalayim
readings.subtitle: The precise registry of the heads of fathers' houses who re-established civil and spiritual architecture within Yerushalayim.
readings.text: [13] and Beri‛ah and Shema, who were heads of their fathers’ houses of the inhabitants of Ayalon, who drove out <dn>את</dn> the inhabitants of Gath. [14] and Aḥyo, Shashaq, and Yerěmoth, [15] and Zeḇaḏyah, and Araḏ, and Ěḏer, [16] and Miḵa’ěl, and Yispah, and Yoḥa were the sons of Beri‛ah. [17] And Zeḇaḏyah, and Meshullam, and Ḥizqi, and Ḥeḇer, [18] and Yishmerai, and Yizli’ah, and Yoḇaḇ were the sons of Elpa‛al. [19] And Yaqim, and Ziḵri, and Zaḇdi, [20] and Eli‛ěynai, and Tsillethai, and Eli’ěl, [21] and Aḏayah, and Berayah, and Shimrath were the sons of Shim‛i. [22] And Yishpan, and Ěḇer, and Eli’ěl, [23] and Aḇdon, and Ziḵri, and Ḥanan, [24] and Ḥananyah, and Ěylam, and Antothiyah, [25] and Yiphdeyah, and Penu’ěl were the sons of Shashaq. [26] And Shamsherai, and Sheḥaryah, and Athalyah, [27] and Ya‛areshyah, and Ěliyah, and Ziḵri were the sons of Yeroḥam. [28] These were heads of the fathers’ houses by their generations, heads. These dwelt in Yerushalayim.
